dismissed.why_not_material: This finding concerns the Phase 1/2 study (NCT06151288) and the rationale for advancing VAX-31 to Phase 3. It critiques the use of OPA as a basis for advancement, but does not pertain to the catalyst trial (NCT07284654) itself. Per principle #2, trial-specific findings only count if they describe the catalyst trial. The critique here is about an earlier-stage study's design logic, not masking of the Phase 3 results.

This operational masking finding concerns VAX-24 (a different program, NCT05844423, an infant vaccine study), not VAX-31 or the adult Phase 3 catalyst trial (NCT07284654). Per principle #2, trial-specific findings are only material if they concern the catalyst trial. This is a different molecule and indication.

This finding identifies a trial identity mismatch: the company attributed N=802 (from the VAX-24 infant trial NCT05844423) to the VAX-31 adult Phase 3 catalyst trial (NCT07284654). While notable, this appears to be a labeling error in marketing materials (conflating two parallel studies) rather than intentional masking of the catalyst trial's enrollment or progress. The catalyst trial's actual registered enrollment (4000) was publicly available. This is careless IR, not deceptive masking of the catalyst readout's likelihood.

analyst_note: All six refuted findings concern either the Phase 1/2 study (claims about OPA surrogacy, cross-trial GMR comparisons to PCV20) or a different program entirely (VAX-24 infant trial timeline). None constitute masking of the adult Phase 3 VAX-31 catalyst trial (NCT07284654). The one moderate-severity finding (pcvx_044) critiques the scientific basis for Phase 3 advancement—standard early-stage promotion, not concealment of pivotal trial design or results. The trial-identity mismatch (pcvx_015, attributing infant-trial enrollment to the adult trial) appears to be an IR labeling error rather than intentional obfuscation of the catalyst's progress. No company-level honesty flags (fraud, misconduct) are present. The marketing is consistent with a sponsor promoting Phase 1/2 immunogenicity data in the run-up to a pivotal readout—normal biotech IR, not masking of a likely miss.
